standard_prerequisites.name: Jacobian criterion for a quotient by an element whose derivative is a unit along the quotient

core_obligations: Note that the polynomial ring over a regular ring is regular (proof lines 11852-11853).
Extend the derivation to the polynomial ring by sending the variable to zero (proof lines 11854-11856).
Apply the quotient criterion, noting that the derivation kills integer polynomials and sends the prescribed element to a unit (proof lines 11855-11857).
proof_roadmap: Regularity of the polynomial ring (proof lines 11852-11853).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that if a regular ring admits a derivation sending a fixed element to a unit, then adjoining a root of a polynomial in that element with integer coefficients preserves regularity. The proof uses that the polynomial ring over a regular ring is regular, extends the given derivation to the polynomial ring by sending the variable to zero, and applies the Jacobian criterion for quotients by a single element, which is available because the extended derivation sends the prescribed element to a unit.
